item.statement: Hot swaging of sintered HfNbTaTiZr specimens failed due to cracking, even when the sample was enveloped in a titanium alloy to maintain temperature.
item.lever: swaging temperature, strain rate, or use of a protective envelope
quotes: This method does not result in a full density alloy due to cracking during swaging.
Unfortunately, the same result was obtained and the specimens were damaged, i.e., cracking occurred as well.
It is also possible that the deformation temperature was too low and the strain rate was too high for the given specimens.

item.statement: Mechanical alloying produces nanocrystalline grains but introduces high oxygen content, leading to brittleness and oxide formation.
item.lever: initial powder type (mechanical alloying vs. gas atomization)
quotes: The MA powder exhibited rather high oxygen content of ≈1.07 wt %, which was ten times higher than that in the AT powder.
Oxygen incorporated into the HfNbTaTiZr samples caused deterioration of mechanical properties (embrittlement) and prevented formation of a single phase random solid solution.

item.statement: Hot Isostatic Pressing (HIP) at 1400 °C and 190 MPa failed to fully eliminate residual porosity in sintered specimens.
quotes: The HIP process caused a slight decrease in porosity, but the specimens still remained rather porous, as seen in Figure 4 c.

The fact that even HIP processing at 1400 °C/200 MPa/2 h did not remove the porosity completely can be ascribed to a high volume fraction of pores and to filling of the pores by Ar gas used as a pressing medium in HIP processing.
However, this decrease was quite small and considerable porosity remained in the specimen.

item.statement: The reason why the hardness of the HEAP-HIP-S specimen did not reach the values of the HEAP-S and HEAP-S-HIP specimens remains unexplained.
item.lever: processing route or phase composition optimization
quotes: However, the hardness of HEAP-HIP-S still did not reach the values of HEAP-S and HEAP-S-HIP.
The cause of this effect remains unclear to the authors.
One can see in Figure 4 c that Ta and Nb rich particles were not fully dissolved during HIP and therefore this specimen was somewhat between a blend of powders and a high entropy alloy.

item.statement: High Pressure Torsion (HPT) processing of mechanically alloyed SPS specimens caused the sample to crack and separate into pieces.
item.lever: sample preparation method or HPT parameters
quotes: It should be accentuated that the MA-SPS specimen was damaged during the HPT process, as many cracks emerged, and the specimen was separated into several smaller pieces.
It should be pointed out that the MA-SPS-HPT specimen was broken into several pieces during the HPT process and therefore the results of such specimen are disputable.
In such cases, the HPT after cracking could not introduce full deformation (strain) to the specimen.

item.statement: While SPS of atomized powder yields a fully dense, single-phase alloy, the subsequent HPT deformation requires a sample that is already free of porosity to avoid cracking.
item.lever: oxygen content and initial powder processing
quotes: Spark plasma sintering (SPS) of mechanically alloyed powders resulted in a fully dense but brittle specimen.
The most promising result was obtained by SPS treatment of gas atomized powder with low oxygen content.

It was reported that the high entropy effect may result into higher hardness since various radii of atoms occupying randomly lattice sites cause random fluctuations of potential energy landscape, which hinders motion of dislocations.

quotes: It should be pointed out that the possibility of hot deformation of the alloy with increased oxygen content cannot be excluded under suitable conditions (i.e., low strain rate, or higher processing temperature) [ [41] ], but this possibility needs more detailed study.

item.statement: Hardness measurements on swaged specimens may be inaccurate because the indent size was affected by the opening of existing cracks.
quotes: However, it should be accentuated that the specimen was damaged during swaging and therefore this hardness value may not be representative.
If the indent was made in the region containing a crack, then it became larger due to a lateral shift of the material caused by opening of the crack.
As a consequence the determined hardness value was lower than in the region without the crack.
